name: PLESS
aliases: Proscar Long-Term Efficacy and Safety Study
question: Does finasteride reduce symptoms, acute urinary retention, and BPH surgery compared with placebo in men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement?

design.population: 3,040 men with moderate-to-severe urinary symptoms and enlarged prostate glands.
design.locator: McConnell 1998 PubMed abstract, Methods; Wessells 2003 publisher abstract, Methods (arm denominators)

verdictNote: Event benefits were assessed in 3,016 evaluable men; symptom change was reported among completers.
takeaway: Four years of finasteride 5 mg daily versus placebo reduced BPH surgery (69/1,513 versus 152/1,503) and acute urinary retention (42/1,513 versus 99/1,503) in men with symptomatic prostatic enlargement; symptom scores also improved among completers.

reports.label: Four-year randomized report
reports.citation: McConnell JD, Bruskewitz R, Walsh P, et al. "The Effect of Finasteride on the Risk of Acute Urinary Retention and the Need for Surgical Treatment among Men with Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *N Engl J Med.* 1998;338(9):557-563. doi:10.1056/NEJM199802263380901

results.measure: Mean symptom-score decrease among study completers; 1–34 symptom-score scale
results.note: The abstract does not state the prespecified primary threshold.
Risk ratio and CI are the inverse of the reported 55% risk reduction (95% CI 41–65%).
Risk ratio and CI are the inverse of the reported 57% risk reduction (95% CI 40–69%).

values.exp: Finasteride 5 mg orally daily for 4 years

delivery.label: Outcome ascertainment
delivery.value: Symptoms, flow, and clinical events assessed every 4 months in 3,016 evaluable men; complete event data in 2,760.

reports.label: Baseline PSA and prostate-volume analysis

results.measure: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve

results.note: Cumulative incidence estimates; event numerators are not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Table I and Results, pp 475–476, Figures 1B and 2A

results.locator: Full text, Table I and Results, pp 475–476, Figures 1B and 2C

results.endpoint: Acute urinary retention or BPH surgery by prostate-volume tertile
results.measure: Four-year cumulative incidence across lowest to highest volume tertiles in MRI subset (n=312)
results.note: Reported finasteride risk reduction ranged from 50% to 74%; no interval or event numerators reported.
